sections.h2: Where is West Springfield, MA, and why is it called the West Side?
sections.html:
West Springfield sits in Hampden County on the west bank of the Connecticut River, directly across from Springfield. Locals call it the West Side for that reason, and the city bills itself as the Crossroads of New England.

It covers 17.54 square miles, of which 16.73 are land, and had 28,835 residents in the 2020 Census. The Westfield River runs along its southern side, and a ridge of volcanic trap rock called East Mountain, part of the Metacomet Ridge, forms the western boundary. Hartford is about 27 miles away and Boston about 90.

West Springfield was incorporated as a town in 1774 after more than a century of friction over crossing the river to reach Springfield's meetinghouse, and it became a city in 2000. The first settlers farmed good land on the west bank, and market gardening grew around Riverdale Road from the 1830s.

Rail changed the town next. The Western Railroad arrived in 1841, and for decades the railroad was one of the largest employers, with rail yards in Mittineague and near Memorial Avenue. Paper mills clustered along the Westfield River, including Southworth Paper, Agawam Paper and Strathmore. Holyoke split off in 1850 and Agawam in 1855, which is why the city's map looks smaller than its colonial territory.

sections.h2: Does flooding or storm history affect a West Springfield house?
sections.html:
Yes, water and weather are a documented part of the city's past, so buyers and insurers ask about them. The Westfield River flooded the town in 1936, when 8,000 people were displaced out of about 17,000. The 1938 hurricane flooded crops along Riverdale Road, and the floods of 1955 came with Hurricanes Connie and Diane five days apart.

More recent events were just as serious:

  • On June 1, 2011, a tornado touched down in West Springfield before crossing the river into Springfield, and two people died in the city.
  • On October 29, 2011, a wet snowstorm brought down limbs and wires, and some homes waited more than a week for power.
  • Dikes now protect low neighborhoods, and the 1950s highway work reinforced them.

If your house is near the river or the dikes, gather any flood insurance records and repair receipts. Those papers answer the first questions a buyer will ask.

sections.h2: Which West Springfield neighborhoods do listings mention?
sections.html:
West Springfield is a city of named districts rather than one downtown. Wikipedia lists Amostown, Ashleyville, Cayenne, Downtown (also called Center), Memorial, Merrick, Mittineague and Tatham. Memorial surrounds Memorial Avenue and the Big E fairgrounds, Ashleyville sits near I-91 and Riverdale Street, and Mittineague lies on the north bank of the Westfield River.

The Eastern States Exposition, known as the Big E, started in 1917 and is the city's biggest tourist draw. The former Eastern States Farmers' Exchange headquarters now serves as West Springfield Town Hall.

sections.h2: How do roads and buses connect West Springfield?
sections.html:
Interstate 91 crosses the northeast part of town, the Massachusetts Turnpike (I-90) passes through, and U.S. 5 (Riverdale Street), U.S. 20 (Westfield Street) and Route 147 (Memorial Avenue) run through it. Pioneer Valley Transit Authority buses link the city to Springfield and to Westfield State University, and Amtrak serves Springfield.

There is no airport in the city. Bradley International in Windsor Locks, Connecticut, is the nearest with commercial flights, while Westover Metropolitan Airport and Westfield-Barnes Regional Airport handle general aviation. Highway access is a real selling point for a commuter, and highway noise is something to mention honestly if your street is close to the ramps.

sections.h2: How should winter weather and storms shape repairs before a sale?
sections.html:
Snow and ice are part of West Springfield's record, and roofs and trees take the brunt. The Great Blizzard of 1888 dropped over 5 feet of snow with 20-foot drifts, and blizzards followed in 1978 and 1996. The October 2011 storm snapped limbs because trees still held their leaves.

Before listing, walk the property with these in mind:

  • Look for ice-dam stains on ceilings and along exterior walls.
  • Check large limbs that hang over the roof or service lines.
  • Test the sump pump if the basement is below the neighborhood grade.

A buyer paying cash may skip these fixes and adjust the price, which can be simpler than repairing a house you plan to leave.

sections.h2: How are property tax abatements handled in West Springfield?
sections.html:
West Springfield assessors follow the state process that the Appellate Tax Board describes. Taxpayers can seek an abatement when the assessed value is higher than fair cash value, the price a willing buyer and seller would agree on without pressure, or when an exemption or classification is wrong.

  • The valuation date is January 1 before the fiscal year starts on July 1.
  • Apply to the assessors by the first payment due date shown on your bill.
  • The assessors have three months to answer, and silence counts as denial.
  • Appeal to the Appellate Tax Board within three months after that.

The city's assessors and collector post their own dates and forms, so ask them which installment schedule applies to your bill.

sections.h2: What does a West Springfield seller pay at closing?
sections.html:
The seller usually pays the deed excise tax. The Hampden County Registry of Deeds states the effective rate as $4.56 per $1,000 of taxable value or fraction of $1,000, with no tax when the stated price is under $100. Its fee for recording a deed is $155, and it takes cash or checks.

On a $300,000 sale, $4.56 times 300 comes to $1,368 in excise tax. Other closing items, such as a payoff, title work and a municipal lien certificate, depend on the property. The Hampden registry lists a municipal lien certificate at $80, which gives you a sense of scale for small charges.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a West Springfield house quickly
sections.html:
A West Springfield owner can list with an agent, sell privately, or take a cash offer from an investor. Listing works well when the house is in good shape and you can wait out showings and a buyer's financing. A cash offer fits when the house has deferred repairs, flood or storm damage, tenants or probate issues.

Whichever route you pick, ask for the contract in writing, check who pays closing costs, and confirm that the buyer can show proof of funds before you commit.

faqs.q: Why is West Springfield called the West Side?
faqs.a: It lies on the west bank of the Connecticut River, across from Springfield, so people shortened it to the West Side. Early residents had to cross the river by boat to reach Springfield's meetinghouse.

faqs.q: How much is the deed excise tax in Hampden County?
faqs.a: The Hampden registry lists the rate as $4.56 per $1,000 of taxable value or fraction of $1,000. A $200,000 sale would carry $912 in excise tax.

faqs.q: Is West Springfield in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Parts of it have flooded repeatedly, including in 1936 and 1955, and dikes now protect low areas. Check the FEMA flood map and your insurance records for your exact address.

faqs.q: What is the Big E and where is it?
faqs.a: The Big E is the Eastern States Exposition, a fall fair that began in 1917 on grounds near Memorial Avenue in West Springfield. It is the city's largest tourist attraction, and the fairgrounds host events through the year.

faqs.q: Which highways run through West Springfield?
faqs.a: Interstate 91, the Massachusetts Turnpike (I-90), U.S. 5, U.S. 20 and Route 147 all pass through the city.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Springfield house with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers, including cash buyers, purchase occupied homes. Read the lease and the Massachusetts tenant guidance first, and ask the buyer in writing how they will handle the tenancy.
